name: Session Restore
location: Firefox (older): sessionstore.js ; Firefox (newer): sessionstore.jsonlz4, sessionstore-backups\ ; Chrome/Edge (older): Current Session, Current Tabs, Last Session, Last Tabs files in the profile root ; Chrome/Edge (newer): Sessions\ folder with Session_<timestamp> / Tabs_<timestamp> files
purpose: Automatic crash-recovery feature that lets the browser restore open tabs and windows after a crash or restart.
key_fields: Historical websites viewed in each tab
normal_baseline: Session-restore data reflects the user's active tabs at the time of the last close or crash, consistent with their known work context.
anomalies: Restored tabs referencing a C2 panel, exfiltration endpoint, or attacker infrastructure open at the time of a crash or shutdown
Session data with form/JavaScript state indicating an in-progress data-exfiltration upload or credential-harvesting page
A Last Session/Last Tabs file present with no matching Current Session, suggesting an abrupt or deliberate browser termination
parsing_tools: Manual JSON review (after jsonlz4/mozLz4 decompression, Firefox)
Manual/hex review of Session_*/Tabs_* files (Chrome/Edge: no universal open-source parser)
anti_forensic_notes: Because these files exist specifically to survive crashes, even a normal, clean browser shutdown can leave the prior session's data in "Last Session"/backup files; fully suppressing this evidence requires clearing both the live session files and profile-level backups (e.g., sessionstore-backups\).
interpretation: Session restore can retain far more than URLs: the actual HTML/JavaScript/XML/form data present on a page, the referring site, transition type (typed, link, reload), window size, and which tabs were pinned. A richer point-in-time capture of browsing state than history alone, useful for reconstructing exactly what was on-screen at shutdown or crash time.
